ko.explanation: 해요체의 종결어미로, 존댓말의 가장 기본적인 표현입니다. 동사나 형용사 뒤에 붙여 공손함을 나타냅니다. 일상 대화에서 가장 많이 쓰이는 존댓말 형태입니다.

examples.intermediate: 처음 만난 사람에게는 "-요"를 써야 해요.
examples.advanced: "-요"는 한국에서 예의를 지킬 때 꼭 필요한 표현입니다.
examples.master: "-요"의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 격식과 친밀함을 적절히 조절할 수 있습니다.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: Why do I have to say it that way?

en.explanation: The most common polite sentence ending in Korean (해요체 / haeyo-che). Added to verbs and adjectives to show politeness. It's the middle level of formality — more polite than casual speech (반말) but softer than formal speech (-습니다).

examples.intermediate: You should use "-요" when meeting someone for the first time.
examples.advanced: "-요" is an essential expression for showing politeness in Korea.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "-요" helps balance formality and familiarity appropriately.

formal: -요 is the polite sentence ending of 해요체.
casual: Just add -요 to make it polite.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why do I have to say it that way?

ko.explanation: 주체 높임 선어말어미 '-시-'와 해요체 '-어요'가 결합한 형태입니다. 상대방의 행동을 높여 말하거나 공손한 요청을 할 때 사용합니다. '가세요', '드세요', '안녕하세요' 등에 쓰입니다.

examples.intermediate: 처음 만난 사람에게는 "-세요"를 써야 해요.
examples.advanced: "-세요"는 한국에서 예의를 지킬 때 꼭 필요한 표현입니다.
examples.master: "-세요"의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 격식과 친밀함을 적절히 조절할 수 있습니다.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: Why do I have to say it that way?

en.explanation: A combination of the subject honorific marker '-시-' and the polite ending '-어요'. Used to elevate the listener's actions or make polite requests. Found in expressions like '가세요' (please go), '드세요' (please eat), and '안녕하세요' (hello).

examples.intermediate: You should use "-세요" when meeting someone for the first time.
examples.advanced: "-세요" is an essential expression for showing politeness in Korea.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "-세요" helps balance formality and familiarity appropriately.

formal: -세요 is the 해요체 form with subject honorification.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why do I have to say it that way?

ko.explanation: 상대방을 높여 부를 때 이름이나 직함 뒤에 붙이는 존칭 접미사입니다. '선생님', '사장님', '손님' 등에 쓰입니다. 인터넷에서는 닉네임 뒤에도 붙입니다.

examples.intermediate: 처음 만난 사람에게는 "님"을 써야 해요.
examples.advanced: "님"은 한국에서 예의를 지킬 때 꼭 필요한 표현입니다.
examples.master: "님"의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 격식과 친밀함을 적절히 조절할 수 있습니다.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: Why do I have to say it that way?

en.explanation: An honorific suffix attached after a name or title to show respect. Used in '선생님' (teacher), '사장님' (boss), '손님' (guest/customer). On the internet, it's commonly added after usernames as a sign of respect.

examples.intermediate: You should use "님" when meeting someone for the first time.
examples.advanced: "님" is an essential expression for showing politeness in Korea.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "님" helps balance formality and familiarity appropriately.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why do I have to say it that way?

ko.explanation: 이름 뒤에 붙여 상대를 보통 수준으로 높이는 호칭입니다. '님'보다 격이 낮고, 주로 성+이름 뒤에 붙입니다. 성만 쓰고 '씨'를 붙이면 무례할 수 있으므로 주의해야 합니다.

examples.intermediate: 처음 만난 사람에게는 "씨"를 써야 해요.
examples.advanced: "씨"는 한국에서 예의를 지킬 때 꼭 필요한 표현입니다.
examples.master: "씨"의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 격식과 친밀함을 적절히 조절할 수 있습니다.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: Why do I have to say it that way?

en.explanation: A moderately polite suffix attached after a person's full name. Less formal than '-님' but polite enough for everyday use. Important: attaching '-씨' after only a surname (e.g., '김 씨') can sound rude; always use the full name (e.g., '김민수 씨').

examples.intermediate: You should use "씨" when meeting someone for the first time.
examples.advanced: "씨" is an essential expression for showing politeness in Korea.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "씨" helps balance formality and familiarity appropriately.

formal: -씨 is a name suffix showing moderate respect.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why do I have to say it that way?

ko.explanation: 상대방을 높여 말하는 말투의 총칭입니다. 반대말은 '반말'(casual speech)입니다. 한국어의 존비어 체계는 세계적으로 가장 복잡한 경어법 중 하나입니다.

examples.intermediate: 처음 만난 사람에게는 "존댓말"을 써야 해요.
examples.advanced: "존댓말"은 한국에서 예의를 지킬 때 꼭 필요한 표현입니다.
examples.master: "존댓말"의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 격식과 친밀함을 적절히 조절할 수 있습니다.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: Why do I have to say it that way?

en.explanation: The general term for polite or formal speech in Korean. The opposite is '반말' (casual speech). Korean has one of the world's most complex honorific systems, with three types: subject, addressee, and object honorification.

examples.intermediate: You should use "존댓말" when meeting someone for the first time.
examples.advanced: "존댓말" is an essential expression for showing politeness in Korea.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "존댓말" helps balance formality and familiarity appropriately.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why do I have to say it that way?

ko.explanation: 높임 표현 없이 편하게 말하는 말투입니다. 친구, 동생, 친한 사이에서 사용합니다. 처음 만난 사람이나 윗사람에게 반말을 쓰면 매우 무례합니다. '말을 놓다'는 반말로 전환하겠다는 뜻입니다.

examples.intermediate: 처음 만난 사람에게는 "반말"을 써야 해요.
examples.advanced: "반말"은 한국에서 예의를 지킬 때 꼭 필요한 표현입니다.
examples.master: "반말"의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 격식과 친밀함을 적절히 조절할 수 있습니다.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: Why do I have to say it that way?

en.explanation: Informal speech without honorific markers, used among friends, younger people, or close relationships. Using 반말 with strangers or elders is considered very rude. The phrase '말을 놓다' means to switch to casual speech.

examples.intermediate: You should use "반말" when meeting someone for the first time.
examples.advanced: "반말" is an essential expression for showing politeness in Korea.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "반말" helps balance formality and familiarity appropriately.

casual: 반말 is how you talk to friends.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why do I have to say it that way?

ko.explanation: 상대방이나 주어를 높여서 말하는 표현의 총칭입니다. 존댓말과 비슷하지만 더 넓은 개념으로, 주체 높임(-시-), 상대 높임(-요, -습니다), 객체 높임(드리다, 여쭙다)을 모두 포함합니다.

examples.intermediate: 처음 만난 사람에게는 "높임말"을 써야 해요.
examples.advanced: "높임말"은 한국에서 예의를 지킬 때 꼭 필요한 표현입니다.
examples.master: "높임말"의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 격식과 친밀함을 적절히 조절할 수 있습니다.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: Why do I have to say it that way?

en.explanation: A general term for speech that elevates the subject or addressee. Broader than 존댓말, it encompasses all three types of Korean honorification: subject honorifics (-시-), addressee honorifics (-요, -습니다), and object honorifics (드리다, 여쭙다).

examples.intermediate: You should use "높임말" when meeting someone for the first time.
examples.advanced: "높임말" is an essential expression for showing politeness in Korea.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "높임말" helps balance formality and familiarity appropriately.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why do I have to say it that way?

ko.explanation: 격식체의 종결어미로, 가장 공손한 존댓말 형태입니다. 뉴스, 발표, 비즈니스 등 공식적인 상황에서 사용합니다. 받침이 있으면 '-습니다', 없으면 '-ㅂ니다'를 씁니다.

examples.intermediate: 처음 만난 사람에게는 "-습니다"를 써야 해요.
examples.advanced: "-습니다"는 한국에서 예의를 지킬 때 꼭 필요한 표현입니다.
examples.master: "-습니다"의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 격식과 친밀함을 적절히 조절할 수 있습니다.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: Why do I have to say it that way?

en.explanation: The most formal and polite sentence ending in Korean (합니다체 / hamnida-che). Used in news broadcasts, presentations, business, and official situations. Use '-습니다' after consonants and '-ㅂ니다' after vowels.

examples.intermediate: You should use "-습니다" when meeting someone for the first time.
examples.advanced: "-습니다" is an essential expression for showing politeness in Korea.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "-습니다" helps balance formality and familiarity appropriately.

casual: -습니다 is the most polite way to speak.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why do I have to say it that way?

ko.explanation: '이다'의 격식체 종결형으로, 자기 소개나 사실을 정중하게 말할 때 사용합니다. '저는 학생입니다', '이것은 책입니다'처럼 명사 뒤에 붙습니다. 해요체 형태는 '-이에요/-예요'입니다.

examples.intermediate: 처음 만난 사람에게는 "-입니다"를 써야 해요.
examples.advanced: "-입니다"는 한국에서 예의를 지킬 때 꼭 필요한 표현입니다.
examples.master: "-입니다"의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 격식과 친밀함을 적절히 조절할 수 있습니다.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: Why do I have to say it that way?

en.explanation: The formal declarative ending of '이다' (to be). Used for polite self-introductions and stating facts. Attached after nouns: '학생입니다' (I am a student), '책입니다' (It is a book). The 해요체 equivalent is '-이에요/-예요'.

examples.intermediate: You should use "-입니다" when meeting someone for the first time.
examples.advanced: "-입니다" is an essential expression for showing politeness in Korea.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "-입니다" helps balance formality and familiarity appropriately.

formal: -입니다 is the formal form of '이다' (to be).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why do I have to say it that way?

ko.explanation: '주다'의 겸양어(겸손 표현)로, 윗사람에게 무엇을 줄 때 사용합니다. 자신을 낮추어 상대를 높이는 객체 높임법의 대표적 표현입니다. '선물을 드리다', '말씀을 드리다' 등으로 씁니다.

examples.intermediate: 처음 만난 사람에게는 "드리다"를 써야 해요.
examples.advanced: "드리다"는 한국에서 예의를 지킬 때 꼭 필요한 표현입니다.
examples.master: "드리다"의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 격식과 친밀함을 적절히 조절할 수 있습니다.

casual: 드리다는 윗사람한테 줄 때 쓰는 말이야.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: Why do I have to say it that way?

en.explanation: The humble form of '주다' (to give), used when giving something to a superior. It's a key example of object honorification where the speaker lowers themselves to elevate the recipient. Used in phrases like '선물을 드리다' (to give a gift) and '말씀을 드리다' (to tell/inform).

examples.intermediate: You should use "드리다" when meeting someone for the first time.
examples.advanced: "드리다" is an essential expression for showing politeness in Korea.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "드리다" helps balance formality and familiarity appropriately.

formal: 드리다 is the humble form of '주다' (to give).
casual: Use 드리다 when giving to someone older or higher-ranked.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why do I have to say it that way?

ko.explanation: '주다'의 주체 높임 표현으로, 윗사람이 아랫사람에게 무엇을 줄 때 사용합니다. '-시-'가 들어가 주어(주는 사람)를 높입니다. '선생님이 주시다', '부모님이 주시다' 등으로 씁니다.

examples.intermediate: 처음 만난 사람에게는 "주시다"를 써야 해요.
examples.advanced: "주시다"는 한국에서 예의를 지킬 때 꼭 필요한 표현입니다.
examples.master: "주시다"의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 격식과 친밀함을 적절히 조절할 수 있습니다.

casual: 주시다는 윗사람이 줄 때 쓰는 말이야.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: Why do I have to say it that way?

en.explanation: The subject-honorific form of '주다' (to give), used when the giver is someone of higher status. The honorific marker '-시-' elevates the subject (the giver). Compare with '드리다' which humbles the giver instead.

examples.intermediate: You should use "주시다" when meeting someone for the first time.
examples.advanced: "주시다" is an essential expression for showing politeness in Korea.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "주시다" helps balance formality and familiarity appropriately.

formal: 주시다 is the subject-honorific form of '주다'.
casual: Use 주시다 when an elder or superior gives something.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why do I have to say it that way?

ko.explanation: '말'의 높임말로, 윗사람의 말을 높이거나 자신의 말을 겸손하게 표현할 때 사용합니다. '선생님의 말씀'(높임), '제가 말씀드리다'(겸양) 두 가지 용법이 있습니다.

examples.intermediate: 처음 만난 사람에게는 "말씀"을 써야 해요.
examples.advanced: "말씀"은 한국에서 예의를 지킬 때 꼭 필요한 표현입니다.
examples.master: "말씀"의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 격식과 친밀함을 적절히 조절할 수 있습니다.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: Why do I have to say it that way?

en.explanation: The honorific form of '말' (words/speech). Has two uses: to elevate a superior's words ('선생님의 말씀' — the teacher's words) or to humble one's own speech ('말씀드리다' — I'd like to say/tell). Context determines which meaning applies.

examples.intermediate: You should use "말씀" when meeting someone for the first time.
examples.advanced: "말씀" is an essential expression for showing politeness in Korea.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "말씀" helps balance formality and familiarity appropriately.

formal: 말씀 is the honorific form of '말' (speech).
casual: 말씀 is the polite way to say '말'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why do I have to say it that way?

ko.explanation: '집'의 높임말로, 상대방의 집을 높여 부를 때 사용합니다. 또한 상대방을 간접적으로 높여 부르는 대명사로도 쓰입니다. '댁에서 오셨어요?'(어디서 오셨어요?의 높임). 전통적이고 격식 있는 표현입니다.

examples.intermediate: 처음 만난 사람에게는 "댁"을 써야 해요.
examples.advanced: "댁"은 한국에서 예의를 지킬 때 꼭 필요한 표현입니다.
examples.master: "댁"의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 격식과 친밀함을 적절히 조절할 수 있습니다.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: Why do I have to say it that way?

en.explanation: The honorific form of '집' (house/home). Used to respectfully refer to someone's house or as an indirect second-person pronoun. '댁이 어디세요?' can mean both 'Where is your home?' and 'Where are you from?' A traditional, formal expression mostly used by older generations.

examples.intermediate: You should use "댁" when meeting someone for the first time.
examples.advanced: "댁" is an essential expression for showing politeness in Korea.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "댁" helps balance formality and familiarity appropriately.

formal: 댁 is the honorific form of '집' (house).
casual: 댁 is the polite way to say someone's house.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why do I have to say it that way?

ko.explanation: '나이'의 높임말로, 어른의 나이를 여쭐 때 사용합니다. '나이'를 직접 사용하면 버릇없게 들릴 수 있으므로, 윗사람에게는 반드시 '연세'를 씁니다. '연세가 어떻게 되세요?'가 올바른 표현입니다.

examples.intermediate: 처음 만난 사람에게는 "연세"를 써야 해요.
examples.advanced: "연세"는 한국에서 예의를 지킬 때 꼭 필요한 표현입니다.
examples.master: "연세"의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 격식과 친밀함을 적절히 조절할 수 있습니다.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: How do you speak in this situation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.translation: Why do I have to say it that way?

en.explanation: The honorific form of '나이' (age). Must be used when asking about an elder's age, as using '나이' directly can sound rude. The standard polite question is '연세가 어떻게 되세요?' (How old are you? — honorific).

examples.intermediate: You should use "연세" when meeting someone for the first time.
examples.advanced: "연세" is an essential expression for showing politeness in Korea.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "연세" helps balance formality and familiarity appropriately.

formal: 연세 is the honorific form of '나이' (age).
casual: 연세 is the polite way to ask about someone's age.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How do you speak in this situation?

translations.ko: 나이가 많은 분을 높여 부르는 말
translations.en: Elder; senior (respectful term for an elderly person)

translations.ko: 편지나 공문에서 상대방을 높여 부르는 말
translations.en: Esteemed person; Dear Sir/Madam (used in letters and official documents)
Your Majesty (highest royal honorific for a king or emperor)
Your Highness (royal honorific for a prince or royal family member)

translations.ko: 대통령이나 고위 관직자를 높여 부르는 말
translations.en: Your Excellency (honorific for a president or high-ranking official)

translations.ko: 동사나 형용사에 붙어 주어를 높이는 선어말 어미
translations.en: Honorific infix added to verbs/adjectives to show respect to the subject

translations.ko: '이/가'의 높임말로, 주어를 높일 때 쓰는 조사
translations.en: Honorific subject marker (respectful equivalent of 이/가)

translations.ko: '에게'의 높임말로, 높여야 할 대상에게 쓰는 조사
translations.en: Honorific dative particle meaning 'to/for' (respectful equivalent of 에게)

translations.ko: '나'의 낮춤말로, 윗사람 앞에서 자신을 가리키는 말
translations.en: I/me (humble form, used when speaking to someone of higher status)

translations.ko: '우리'의 낮춤말로, 윗사람 앞에서 자기 쪽을 가리키는 말
translations.en: We/our (humble form, used when speaking to someone of higher status)

translations.ko: '묻다'의 겸양어로, 윗사람에게 물을 때 쓰는 말
translations.en: To ask (humble form, used when asking someone of higher status)

translations.ko: '보다'의 겸양어로, 윗사람을 만날 때 쓰는 말
translations.en: To see/meet (humble form, used when meeting someone of higher status)
To serve, attend to, or accompany (someone of higher status)

translations.ko: 상대방을 높여 말하는 언어 표현의 총칭
translations.en: Respectful language; honorific speech (general term for polite/formal language)
Humble language; self-deprecating speech used to elevate the listener
Form of address; title or name used to call or refer to someone
